retained_completed_reviews.proof_scope: Projected energy is C1 under every continuous real perturbation, with any relative finite-energy base. Finite-integral variational maximizers are exactly prescribed-measure solutions. Bounded-density measures of matching reference mass admit normalized relative E1 solutions. Every positive-parameter exponential full-mass solution dominates a supersolution for any finite non-pluripolar measure; hence it is unique. Bounded-density exponential measures admit a unique relative E1 variational solution. General non-pluripolar existence, unweighted uniqueness and relative boundedness estimates remain unproved here.

Fixed-background L1 convergence has the expected quasi-everywhere upper limit; bounded potentials converge in L1 of any fixed finite non-pluripolar measure. Exponentials have a common bounded quasi-psh background and converge in measure L1. Positive-mass model references in big classes admit unique full-mass solutions of every positive exponential equation, which are relative E1 variational maximizers. Lower bounds by densities converging almost everywhere survive volume L1 potential limits. Sending the exponential parameter to zero produces normalized full-mass solutions for arbitrary non-pluripolar measures of matching mass. Unweighted uniqueness is not claimed.

For every pair of bounded relative-type obstacles and positive parameter, there is a unique relative full-mass solution of the two-obstacle exponential equation. It has bounded relative type, is below their rooftop and dominates any full-mass supersolution. Solutions increase with the parameter and differ from the rooftop by at most (D+n log(2 lambda))/lambda for lambda at least one, off the poles. Energy and measures converge. This proves the supplied auxiliary equation without assuming finite untruncated coefficient mass.

A cutoff Riesz decomposition gives finite-p disc norms controlled by a finite negative center; Tonelli in coordinate variables and a selected center give local Lp/L1 estimates and all-finite-p convergence. Fixed smooth background and normalized compactness give uniform global Lp norms. For a positive-mass model in a big class, residual measure domination mu_u<=nu+a mu_phi, a<1, and superlinear capacity domination imply bounded relative type, with an explicit moment-depth constant. Full-mass sublevel tails and comparison precede a geometric finite-extinction iteration; relative domination upgrades the measure conclusion pointwise. Energy sublevels and Lp densities with the explicitly retained capacity hypothesis give quantitative corollaries.
